findings.title: Enforce the 95% coverage floor in CI; all four packages are below it

locations.snippet: ≥95% coverage ... Below 95% is a **failed** task — not a warning.
| Coverage floor / Packagist API | **Not** enforced here (unit exit codes only ...) |

findings.current_state: AGENTS.md calls 95% line coverage blocking, but CI installs PHP with `coverage: none`, no composer script measures it, and Go runs plain `go test`. Measured today (PHP 8.5 + pcov, `pest --coverage --min=95`): core 92.5%, messaging 91.4%, AI 89.1%. Go CLI: 88.5% total (`go tool cover -func`), with helpfmt at 78.4% and flagschema at 83.6%. The suites are green, but every package misses the floor.
findings.recommended_state: CI runs PHP with pcov and `pest --coverage --min=95` for each package, and Go with a coverage-profile threshold. A PR that drops a package below the floor fails. If the floor is not realistic yet, lower it in AGENTS.md to the measured value and ratchet it up.
findings.rationale: The policy is enforced only by agent discipline, and it has drifted 3–6.5 points under the bar on every package. The prior audit's X-005 was deferred in UR-012 as polish. Measurement now shows the stated gate is false, not just unchecked, so severity stays high: docs and agents assert a guarantee the repo does not meet.
findings.implementation_hint: tests.yml php job: set `coverage: pcov`. Add composer scripts `test:core:coverage` = `pest --configuration=packages/laravel-capabilities/phpunit.xml --coverage --min=95` (and the same for messaging and AI), then call them from CI. Go job: `go test -coverprofile=c.out ./... && go tool cover -func=c.out | awk '/^total:/ {sub("%","",$3); if ($3+0 < 95) exit 1}'`. Then close the gap with real tests, or delete dead paths, before turning the gate on.

findings.title: Add LICENSE (and SECURITY.md) to the split laravel-capabilities-ai package

locations.snippet: no LICENSE, no SECURITY.md (core, messaging, cli each have both)

findings.current_state: split-packages.yml mirrors `packages/laravel-capabilities-ai` to the public rawphp/laravel-capabilities-ai repo, and v* tags are force-pushed there too. That tree has no LICENSE file and no SECURITY.md. The root SECURITY.md lists only the other three packages as report targets.
findings.recommended_state: The AI package root carries the same MIT LICENSE and a package SECURITY.md as its siblings. Root SECURITY.md names all four packages.
findings.rationale: MIT requires the copyright and permission notice to ship with the software. Composer metadata alone does not satisfy that, and GitHub shows the public repo as unlicensed. The package also has no private vulnerability-report path, even though it holds the Anthropic LLM client and turn endpoints.
findings.implementation_hint: cp packages/laravel-capabilities-messaging/LICENSE packages/laravel-capabilities-ai/; adapt packages/laravel-capabilities-messaging/SECURITY.md into the AI package; add `laravel-capabilities-ai` to the list at root SECURITY.md:20. Optional: a unit test in the AI package's tests/Unit/Architecture that asserts is_file(LICENSE) && is_file(SECURITY.md), mirroring the existing DocsTest.

findings.title: Split PHP package repos ship a test suite that cannot run outside the monorepo
findings.current_state: The split mirrors tests/, phpunit.xml and a `composer test` script into each PHP package remote. The bootstraps and Pest.php require `dirname(package,2)/vendor/autoload.php`. The AI bootstrap loads core from `packages/laravel-capabilities/src`. Core architecture and doc tests read `docs/spec.md`, `docs/requirements-inventory.md`, the root README and sibling composer.json through MONOREPO_ROOT. In a split clone, `composer install && composer test` fatals at bootstrap. No package has a .gitattributes, so Packagist dist archives also include tests/, docs/ and phpunit.xml.
findings.recommended_state: Pick one: (a) the split excludes monorepo-only test scaffolding (tests/, phpunit.xml, `scripts.test`) and each package gets `.gitattributes` export-ignore; or (b) the bootstraps fall back to the package-local vendor and monorepo-coupled tests are skipped when MONOREPO_ROOT is absent. Package READMEs say to contribute through the monorepo.
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md requires packages to be self-contained after the split. Right now a contributor or auditor who clones a public package repo gets a broken `composer test`, and PRs on those repos have no CI. Option (a) is the smaller change and keeps the monorepo as the one test authority. The CLI shows the working pattern: its Go tests run standalone in its own release.yml.
findings.implementation_hint: split-packages.yml rsync: add `--exclude 'tests/' --exclude 'phpunit.xml'` for PHP paths only (the matrix entry can carry an `excludes` field, since the CLI must keep *_test.go). Remove `scripts.test` from the three package composer.json files, or point it at a message. Add packages/*/.gitattributes with `/tests export-ignore`, `/phpunit.xml export-ignore`, `/docs export-ignore` (the prior X-011 is still open).

findings.title: Constrain sibling packages' core requirement instead of "*"

locations.snippet: breaking changes may land without a `1.0.0` major bump (SemVer allows this on 0.x)

findings.current_state: Messaging and AI accept any core version. Twenty lockstep v* tags (v0.1.1 through v0.5.3) are already pushed to every package remote. The AI package uses core APIs that change between 0.x minors (CapabilityBus::invoke, CapabilityResult, error envelope, agent_turn budget).
findings.recommended_state: Each sibling requires the core minor it was built with, e.g. `"rawphp/laravel-capabilities": "^0.5.3"` (caret on 0.x means >=0.5.3 <0.6.0). The release script bumps it with each tag. A unit test asserts the constraint is not `*`.
findings.rationale: With lockstep tags and 0.x breaking minors, `*` lets Composer pair, for example, messaging v0.3.0 with core v0.5.3, or a future core 1.x with today's siblings. Nothing flags the mismatch, and the resulting breaks are hard to trace. Each tag should be a tested set.
findings.implementation_hint: In scripts/release.sh, after computing NEW_TAG, rewrite both sibling require entries to `^${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}` with php -r or jq, then commit before tagging. In the monorepo, the root path repositories with `*@dev` still resolve because of branch-alias `0.x-dev`; check that `composer update` still links the path packages, or add `"version"` to the path repo options. Extend the existing AI ArchitectureTest (which already reads composer.json) with `expect($composer['require']['rawphp/laravel-capabilities'])->not->toBe('*')`.

findings.title: Invert core → AI coupling in integration-health (class-string + config probes)
findings.current_state: Core hard-codes four AI-package FQCNs, the AI config shape (`capabilities-ai.routes.enabled`, `queue.name`), an `isReady()` method name, and a class-name substring check for `AlwaysReady`. Core tests use the same literal strings, so nothing fails if the AI package renames or moves a contract. The health check would then silently report 'unbound' or 'skipped'. The architecture test only checks core's composer.json, not these source-level references.
findings.recommended_state: Dependencies point sibling → core only. Core defines a small `IntegrationHealthContributor` contract (checks(): list of rows). The AI package registers its contributor (container tag), and integration-health iterates the tagged contributors. Core then holds no AI names, and the D-024 placement of the command in core is unchanged. Minimum alternative: an AI-package unit test that asserts each core constant resolves (`interface_exists(IntegrationHealthChecker::AI_CONTEXT)` etc.) and that `AlwaysReadyIdempotency` matches the substring check.
findings.rationale: D-007 and D-024 keep core thin, with siblings depending on core contracts. String probes make core the one place that must track AI internals, which is the wrong direction. It is also invisible to static analysis and to the existing 'core does not require AI' test. Because the failure mode is a readiness check that passes silently, the diagnostic stops protecting hosts from the unsafe AlwaysReady binding it exists to catch.
findings.implementation_hint: Fast guard (trivial): add packages/laravel-capabilities-ai/tests/Unit/Architecture/CoreHealthProbeTest.php that asserts interface_exists for IntegrationHealthChecker::AI_CONTEXT, AI_TOOL_CATALOG, 'Rawphp\\CapabilitiesAi\\Contracts\\IdempotencyReadiness' and ProgressStoreReadiness, plus method_exists(ProgressStoreReadiness::class,'isReady'). Structural fix (small): add Rawphp\\Capabilities\\Contracts\\IntegrationHealthContributor, have CapabilitiesAiServiceProvider tag its implementation, and move the checkAiChat/progress logic into the AI package.

findings.title: Run Pint and PHPStan in CI; PHPStan is installed but never configured or run

locations.snippet: PHPStan max on package code when CI lands.
run: composer test   (only PHP gate step)

findings.current_state: CI and scripts/release.sh run only the Pest and Go suites. Pint passes today (`composer format:test` → passed) but is not gated. PHPStan is in root and core require-dev, but there is no phpstan.neon anywhere, no composer script, and no CI step. Messaging and AI don't declare it. The prior X-008 is still open.
findings.recommended_state: The tests.yml php job runs `composer format:test` and `composer analyse` (phpstan.neon at root with paths for all three package src dirs, at a level that passes today plus a baseline). release.sh runs the same commands.
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md makes PHPStan max a stated goal once CI exists, and CI now exists. Without a gate, an unused dev dependency signals safety the repo does not have. X-005 (string class probes) is exactly the kind of drift static analysis plus a custom rule could flag.
findings.implementation_hint: Add phpstan.neon: `parameters: { level: 6, paths: [packages/laravel-capabilities/src, packages/laravel-capabilities-messaging/src, packages/laravel-capabilities-ai/src] }`, generate a baseline with `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --generate-baseline`, and add the composer script `"analyse": "phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G"`. In tests.yml, add steps `composer format:test` and `composer analyse` before `composer test`. Mirror them in the scripts/release.sh gates.

findings.title: CI tests only Laravel 12 on PHP 8.2; add the declared 11/13 and 8.3+ cells
findings.current_state: CI runs one cell: PHP 8.2 with the committed lock, which resolves Illuminate 12.64. Laravel 11 and 13, and PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, are declared supported but never exercised. A local run on PHP 8.5 already surfaces deprecations CI never sees (e.g. ReflectionProperty::setAccessible in CoverageBoost2Test.php:580).
findings.recommended_state: A small matrix in tests.yml: {php 8.2, laravel 11 prefer-lowest}, {php 8.3, laravel 12}, {php 8.4, laravel 13}. Each cell runs `composer update illuminate/*:^N --with-all-dependencies` before the suites.
findings.rationale: The packages are published libraries that promise a three-major Illuminate range. Framework API drift across 11→13 (container, routing, validation, query builder signatures used by QueryTableGateway) will only show up in consumer apps. Matrix cells are cheap because the suite is unit-only and DB-free.
findings.implementation_hint: In tests.yml: `strategy.matrix.include: [{php: '8.2', illuminate: '^11.0', stability: 'prefer-lowest'}, {php: '8.3', illuminate: '^12.0', stability: 'prefer-stable'}, {php: '8.4', illuminate: '^13.0', stability: 'prefer-stable'}]`, then `composer require "illuminate/support:${{ matrix.illuminate }}" --no-update && composer update --${{ matrix.stability }} --with-all-dependencies`. Keep the lockfile cell as the default fast job.

findings.title: Package CHANGELOGs lag the 20+ lockstep tags; core has two [Unreleased] blocks

locations.snippet: ### Added   (second Added heading inside the first [Unreleased], see line 14)
## [Unreleased] ... ## [0.x]   (no version sections; GitHub Releases cut per tag)
fill dated CHANGELOG sections when cutting each tag.

findings.current_state: Tags v0.1.1–v0.5.3 are force-pushed to all four package remotes. Only core has dated sections (0.5.2, 0.5.3), and core also has a stale second `[Unreleased]` holding shipped work. Messaging and CLI have none. AI stops at 0.5.1. scripts/release.sh never touches CHANGELOGs, even though docs/versioning.md says to fill them per tag.
findings.recommended_state: Each tag produces a dated section in every package CHANGELOG (or an explicit 'No changes' line), and there is exactly one `[Unreleased]` per file. release.sh refuses to tag while `[Unreleased]` is non-empty in any package, or it promotes those sections automatically.
findings.rationale: The package remotes are the consumer-facing products. For 0.x, where breaking changes land on minors, the CHANGELOG is the only upgrade guide. Tags without notes make X-004's pairing problem worse.
findings.implementation_hint: Add a release.sh step: for each packages/*/CHANGELOG.md, replace the first `## [Unreleased]` with `## [Unreleased]\n\n## [X.Y.Z] - $(date +%F)` and fail if a file has more than one `## [Unreleased]`. Fix the core file by merging lines 146+ into the correct released section.

findings.title: Point Dependabot at the CLI's nested release workflow
findings.current_state: The github-actions updater scans only /.github/workflows. The CLI's release workflow handles signing keys (CAPABILITIES_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY, Apple and Windows certs) and lives under packages/capabilities-cli/.github/workflows, so it never gets update PRs in the monorepo. The split child repo has no dependabot.yml either.
findings.recommended_state: dependabot.yml covers both workflow roots, so action bumps for the release pipeline arrive as monorepo PRs and flow to the child through the split.
findings.rationale: This is the only workflow that holds long-lived signing secrets. Stale action versions there carry the most supply-chain risk, and it is the one location the current config misses.
findings.implementation_hint: Change the github-actions entry to `directories: ["/", "/packages/capabilities-cli"]` (Dependabot supports `directories` for multi-root configs).

findings.title: Reconcile requirements inventory: stale CLI mcp rows, AI package absent
findings.current_state: `python3 tools/report_inventory_gaps.py` reports 2 unmatched rows. Both are `mcp` auth-guard scenarios for a CLI command that was hard-removed (help.go:164), yet the inventory marks them [x]. The only live test is `TestMcpwithoutauthfails`. The AI package (≈4.5k LOC, 311 tests) has no inventory rows, and the sync and gap tools don't scan it, even though AGENTS.md treats inventory→tests as the contract scaffold.
findings.recommended_state: The generator catalog drops or renames the two mcp rows. The gap report runs clean and is cheap enough to run in CI. AGENTS.md either states that the AI package is governed by its own tests and README instead of the inventory, or the tools gain an `ai` package entry.
findings.rationale: A gap tool that always reports stale noise stops being read. Checked boxes for tests that don't exist undermine the 'tests are SOT' contract. The tools' own unit tests (31, green) are also not in CI.
findings.implementation_hint: Remove lines 1581 and 2955 from tools/generate_requirement_stubs.py (or map them to TestMcpwithoutauthfails), regenerate, and re-run sync. Add a tests.yml job: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/tests && python3 tools/report_inventory_gaps.py --fail-on-gaps` (add the flag). Add one AGENTS.md line on AI package inventory scope.

notes: Library monorepo: app-level checks skipped (no .env/.env.example needed, no Docker/deploy, no observability/APM, no DB schema beyond package migrations, which package auditors cover). Evidence was gathered by running commands, not only reading: `composer test` is green (core 5172, messaging 352, AI 311 tests); `composer format:test` passes; `pest --coverage --min=95` fails on all three PHP packages (92.5/91.4/89.1, PHP 8.5 + pcov locally; CI uses 8.2, so exact numbers may shift slightly); Go total 88.5%; tools/tests is 31 green. Verified fixed since the 2026-07-31 audit and not re-raised: CI exists (X-001), split gated on tests (X-002), CLI release runs go test (X-003), LICENSE for core/messaging/cli (X-004 partly; AI still missing → X-002), composer.lock committed (X-006), Dependabot added (X-009, one gap → X-010), SECURITY.md (X-010), Go pinned to go.mod (X-012), split concurrency (X-013), Pint added (X-016). Still open from the prior audit and re-raised with current evidence: coverage (old X-005, deferred in UR-012; the new measurement shows an actual breach, so it stays high), PHPStan (old X-008), export-ignore (old X-011, folded into X-003). Package doc links: every relative markdown link resolves and none escape the package root (split-safe); absolute monorepo spec anchors match headings. Dependency direction: messaging → core and AI → core only; core → messaging uses a single class_exists presence check (spec-sanctioned, D-007 soft-enable, not flagged); core → AI string probes flagged as X-005 (D-024 places the command in core, so only the coupling mechanism is flagged). Not flagged: AI package relies transitively on core for illuminate/console and routing; `release.sh --squash` force-with-lease history rewrite (explicit maintainer design). For package auditors: core tests include tests/Unit/CoverageGreen/CoverageBoost*Test.php, named for coverage, which is worth checking against the AGENTS.md 'do not game coverage' rule.
